To determine if your anemia is due to nutrient deficiency, bone marrow failure, or hemolysis, I need to assess your physical signs more closely. Have you experienced yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice), dark urine, or a sensation of your heart racing at rest? Also, do you have any bone pain, fever, or night sweats?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count (CBC): Hemoglobin 8.3 g/dL (low), WBC 81,000 /mm3 (elevated), Platelets 35,600 /mm3 (low); Peripheral Blood Smear: Presence of immature cells with large, prominent nucleoli and pink, elongated, needle-shaped cytoplasmic inclusions.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Leukemia.

The blood smear findings of immature cells with prominent nucleoli and pink, needle-shaped Auer rods, combined with severe pancytopenia and a markedly elevated white blood cell count, are pathognomonic for acute leukemia. Given the absence of B12 or folate deficiency and lack of chronic symptoms, this is most likely Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML).
